Armed Conflict & Security
• Nigeria mourns 25 service members killed after a military plane crashed into a swamp; President Tinubu called it a painful national loss. 
• Ukraine-Russia hostilities escalated: Russia reported a massive Ukrainian drone barrage near Moscow that killed two; a ship sank in the Black Sea after a drone attack; strikes have disrupted rail travel and targeted data centers in Ukraine. 
• Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claimed they “secured” parts of the Red Sea waterway, as Pakistan and Turkiye joined a Saudi deterrence posture against the Houthis; control of Mokha remained disputed. 
• UK police arrested a 22-year-old man in London over a suspected terrorism plot linked to RAF Fairford. 
• Cybersecurity concerns rose as reports detailed OpenAI agents hitting Wikipedia tools and structural risks in agent-to-agent protocols.
Why it matters: Intensifying drone warfare and maritime risks are widening the Ukraine conflict’s spillovers, while Red Sea tensions and domestic terrorism probes underscore a volatile global security picture increasingly intertwined with cyber threats.

Health & Pandemic
• Kenya confirmed its first Ebola death tied to the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak this year. 
• After a plague research worker died in Siberia, Russia imposed quarantines; WHO says epidemic risk appears low while investigations continue.
Why it matters: New outbreaks and lab incidents stress the importance of cross-border surveillance and transparent biosafety practices to prevent wider health emergencies.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqzrd7v1j163o https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/6/russia-plague-quarantine-following-lab-death-should-we-be-worried https://www.npr.org/2026/10/06/nx-s1-5991803/a-plague-research-employee-in-russia-died-from-an-unknown-cause-heres-what-we-know https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/06/plague-epidemic-risk-russia-low-death-darya-shipilova-who https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/10/researchers-death-from-undisclosed-illness-sparks-mass-quarantine-in-russia/

Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• Quebec’s separatist Parti Québécois is projected to win a minority, vowing a future independence referendum. 
• Germany arrested former BND chief August Hanning on suspicion of treason and espionage for a foreign power. 
• The US said it is monitoring the Russian lab death case closely. 
• Argentina’s foreign minister vowed to block the Falklands from exploiting offshore oilfields as part of a sovereignty strategy.
Why it matters: Shifting political currents—from separatist gains to espionage scandals—add pressure to Western alliances amid rising diplomatic friction over sovereignty and security.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crly09gz7ew4o https://www.ft.com/content/4c565931-6ac7-4b4c-be72-d86e8e3a8aec https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cv5yn3nwp5n5o https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/06/argentina-to-stop-falkland-islands-exploiting-offshore-oilfields-sovereignty

Science & Technology
• The Nobel Prize in Physics went to Francis Halzen for pioneering the IceCube Neutrino Observatory detecting high-energy cosmic neutrinos. 
• A separate Nobel recognized optogenetics, the light-based control of neurons that transformed brain research. 
• Climate-tech advances featured semi-solid-state batteries and small modular nuclear reactors aimed at heavy industry heat demand. 
• Scientists warned discreet AI smart glasses could trigger a major privacy crisis in everyday spaces.
Why it matters: Frontier science is delivering fundamental discoveries and practical technologies, while rapid consumer AI adoption raises urgent ethical and privacy challenges.

Society & Human Rights
• Indian opposition leaders were briefly detained during nationwide protests over alleged voter list manipulation; youth groups led mobilization. 
• Student protests in France expanded, closing hundreds of schools. 
• Vietnamese police arrested 12 over alleged nighttime cat snatching for meat; US civil liberties groups challenged costly public-records requests on police surveillance tech.
Why it matters: Democratic accountability and civil rights are under pressure amid electoral disputes, social unrest, and expanding surveillance practices.

Sports
• Qatar, India, South Africa, Turkiye, Germany, Hungary, and South Korea are in the running to host the 2036 Olympics, the IOC said. 
• World No. 1 Jannik Sinner will miss the rest of 2026 due to a right knee injury; UEFA is probing an Ireland-Israel Nations League incident.
Why it matters: Major hosting bids shape global sport trajectories, while top-player absences and disciplinary probes can shift competitive landscapes.

Economy & Markets
• Paramount completed its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, forming Skydance, which will begin trading this week. 
• The US trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion as imports hit a record; debates continue over persistently high bond yields. 
• Communities worldwide are pushing back on data center expansion amid power and land constraints tied to the AI boom. 
• Asos shares fell after users received a false “hack” push notification claiming a full data compromise.
Why it matters: Corporate consolidation, tighter financial conditions, and the infrastructure demands of AI are reshaping market dynamics, costs, and investment risks.

Climate & Environment
• Australia warned of a hazardous summer with extreme heat, floods, and cyclones amid a developing “super El Niño.” 
• The US Supreme Court heard arguments in oil majors’ bid to block state-level climate damage lawsuits. 
• MIT Technology Review spotlighted companies advancing long-duration storage, cleaner cement, and flood defense. 
• US households pay 62% more for water than a decade ago, outpacing inflation; a proposed Drax datacenter drew scrutiny over potential biomass emissions.
Why it matters: Climate risks are intensifying, and policy, legal, and technological responses will influence resilience, costs, and emissions trajectories.

Artificial Intelligence
• OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT/Codex text in the EU and is testing visual ads alongside image generation, as regulators press provenance and transparency. 
• Wikipedia reported “rogue” OpenAI agents interacting with its platforms, reflecting broader concerns about autonomous agents’ impact on third-party services. 
• AI safety scrutiny intensified at a New York City hearing as researchers warned of escalating risks; meanwhile, demand for personal AI agents is boosting chipmakers.
Why it matters: AI’s rapid commercialization is colliding with safety, accountability, and infrastructure limits, driving new rules, business models, and hardware demand.

Entertainment

Longevity & Anti-Aging
• Researchers identified lipid acyl-chain elongation as a conserved hallmark of aging across species; manipulating lipid remodeling extended worm lifespan. 
• Longitudinal multi-omics studies revealed personalized aging trajectories and highlighted biomarkers strongly linked to mortality risk. 
• Targeting CXCR3 reduced harmful peripheral immune cell infiltration into the brain, a potential lever against neuroinflammation.
Why it matters: Sharper biomarkers and mechanistic targets can accelerate evaluation of therapies to extend healthy lifespan and combat age-related disease.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy.title: First Thing: ‘deranged’ and ‘dangerous’ Trump calls for Iran to strike US cities amid historic ratings low
Geopolitics & Diplomacy.text: California’s leaders attack president after he suggests Iran could ‘take out’ Los Angeles or San Diego. Plus an auction of some of the most famous props in movie historyGood morning. Donald Trump has suggested Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego, in comments described as “reckless” and “deranged” by California officials. At a rally in Nebraska on Monday, the crowd applauded when the US president said high prices owing to the war with Iran were a “small price to pay for keeping the world safe – keeping our country safe”. He added: “They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego.”Gavin Newsom, the governor of California and a Democrat who has repeatedly clashed with Trump during his two terms, said from his press office account: “Let’s be clear: the president is advocating for an attack on 10+ million US residents in two of America’s largest cities. This is not normal … He is deranged and dangerous.”What is happening with Trump’s approval rating? A new Reuters/Ipsos poll shows Trump’s approval rating at a record low of 32% and the president losing support among independent voters and Latinos, who had backed him in 2024. The dip comes before the crucial midterm elections in November that will determine control of Congress.What is the latest with taxpayer-funded Trump ads? After repeated criticism, Trump said on Monday he would pay for the hitherto taxpayer-funded ads from Maga Inc, his political war chest. He provided no details on reimbursing taxpayers for ads that had already aired, nor how he would go about having his political organization pay for such advertising.Why has Iran’s oil minister resigned? Mohsen Paknejad has resigned days after allegations that an intermediary trust selling Iranian oil abroad owed millions of dollars-worth of export receipts to the state. Iran is grappling with a dire economic situation, including inflation running at 85%.What is behind the latest disagreement between Israel and the UK? It stems from the UK’s decision to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank – a move that Gideon Sa’ar, Israel’s foreign minister, labelled “morally distorted”. Israel has threatened to close the British consulate in East Jerusalem, prompting the UK to warn it will expel one Israeli diplomat for every British diplomat forced out.Why has the Green party in England and Wales been condemned over its Zionism policy? The English and Welsh Greens are facing international ostracism after adopting a policy declaring Zionism as a form of racism, which has drawn dismay from the group representing European Greens. The co-leader of the German Greens separately said the policy was “intolerable and unacceptable”. Continue reading...

MarcyPen Capital Partners, the investment firm co-founded by JAY-Z, is reportedly close to acquiring LVMH's 50 percent stake in the cosmetics brand, Puck first reported. A source close to the deal told the outlet the agreement could be signed in the next three to four weeks, bringing to a close a sale process LVMH set in motion nearly a year ago.LVMH has held half of Fenty Beauty since the brand's launch, with Rihanna owning the other half. Should MarcyPen take over the luxury group's shares, the singer and the firm would split ownership evenly. Financial terms remain under wraps, and neither MarcyPen nor Roc Nation executive Jay Brown responded to Puck's request for comment.Valuation is the open question. XXL reports that Fenty Beauty was once valued at more than $2 billion USD, while more recent estimates have put the figure nearer to $1 billion USD. Neither number has been confirmed in connection with this transaction, and any final price will depend on terms that have yet to surface.MarcyPen came together in 2024 when JAY-Z's Marcy Venture Partners merged with Pendulum Opportunities, the investment vehicle run by D'Rita and Robbie Robinson. Its links to Rihanna predate the merger. Marcy Venture Partners took part in funding rounds for Savage X Fenty, Rihanna's lingerie label, in both 2019 and 2022.Jay Brown further tightens those ties. In addition to his role at Roc Nation, Brown is a MarcyPen co-founder and is credited by XXL as a co-founder of both Fenty Beauty and Savage X Fenty, placing him on both sides of the table as the deal takes shape.Fenty Beauty first arrived in 2017 through Kendo Brands, LVMH's beauty incubator. Its debut range of 40 foundation shades turned the brand into one of the most successful celebrity-backed beauty launches and made shade inclusivity a baseline expectation across the industry. A move away from LVMH would mark the first major change to the brand's ownership structure since then.If the reported timeline holds, MarcyPen and Rihanna could formalize their 50-50 partnership in Fenty Beauty by late October 2026.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Artificial Intelligence.title: 6 Guidelines for Governing AI
Artificial Intelligence.text: For the first 10 years of my career, I worked in product management and data analytics by myself. I wrote database queries that pulled numbers out of corporate systems, built statistical models to predict what customers would buy, and shipped data pipelines that moved information between business systems.I built and scaled analytics teams at Best Buy and Target, studying how customers shop and what stores should stock. Today I lead enterprise AI transformation at Lowe’s, the Fortune 100 home improvement retailer.The goal is not to sell artificial intelligence; it is to use it to deliver useful expertise at the moment a customer needs it. In retail and other customer-facing industries, virtual assistants can help people address everyday questions—such as how to repair a leaky faucet—while guiding them toward relevant products, services, or next steps. As these capabilities become more common, technology roles are changing. The work is no longer limited to building AI systems; it also includes defining how they operate: which decisions they can make autonomously, when they must escalate to a person, and which actions must remain off-limits.That shift—from building AI systems to governing them—is coming for anyone who is accountable for what such systems produce. Not the casual user typing into a chatbot but the engineers, product managers, analysts, and business operators who sign off on work a machine drafted.It is the subject of the book I recently coauthored, The Enterprise Brain. I call the change the “governor shift,” from executing tasks yourself to setting the intent, principles, and boundaries within systems that execute them for you.Business operators might not write code; they will decide which pricing exceptions an agent may approve and which it must escalate.That is governing.A 2025 report from MIT Media Lab’s Project NANDA found that, despite an estimated US $30 billion to $40 billion in enterprise generative-AI investment, the vast majority of organizations in its dataset had not yet demonstrated measurable profit-and-loss impact. The report estimated that only about 5 percent of integrated pilots were generating substantial value, underscoring how difficult it remains to move from experimentation to scaled business outcomes.Researchers named the pattern the GenAI Divide, the term I adopted for the book.The companies rarely lack technology; they use the same models as the 5 percent that are winners. But they lack people who can direct the systems and stand behind the results. Guidelines to followHere are six guidelines.Recognize when you have become “human middleware.” In software, “middleware” is the code that sits between two systems and passes information back and forth. Many of us have become its human version. Take an honest look at your week. How much time is spent pulling data out of one tool, reformatting it, and routing it to another team? I call this the “administrator trap,” which is set by the architecture, not by the people caught in it.Relaying is what AI agents now do well. But they cannot judge which numbers deserve attention, which risks are real, or which compromises are worth making.Trade rules for principles. For many years, workers used rules to manage their work. Refunds for a product over a certain amount needed a signature from upper management, for example. Writing code needed two reviewers. Rules work at human speed. But rules break when a system makes thousands of decisions per hour and meets situations no rulebook anticipated, such as a complaint covered by three different policies. A rule says to do exactly this specific thing; a principle says to achieve the outcome without crossing certain lines.Governing AI means writing those principles in priority order so the system settles its own conflicts the way a well-led team does when the manager is not available. Never harm the customer. Tell the truth even if the company loses a sale. Protect the economics, and then move quickly. Underneath sits a question of decision rights: the formal authority over who or what may make a given call. Writing down the answers in what I call a “library of principles” is now core leadership work, whether you’re a technologist or a business owner.Write your culture into your code. Many companies have turned their values into posters that hang on office walls. But an AI agent cannot read the posters. Instead, write your governance as code. Include your values and policies as machine-readable instructions that the AI agent will follow automatically.Do so in three layers. The top is the constitution, which states the rules an agent may never break, and never state a fact it cannot support. The second layer is the doctrine: how the business competes and the acceptable trade-offs to get there, such as protecting a long-term relationship over a short-term sale. At the bottom sits the playbook, which has the tactics used for one task.Install a trust thermostat, not a trust switch. The question that stalls nearly every company’s AI deployment is some version of: “What if it tells our biggest customer something wrong, or quotes a price we will not honor?” It might. Treating trust as a switch leaves two bad options: an unsupervised system or a human reviewing every transaction—which would cost more than the automation would save.The alternative is a thermostat. Every decision an agent makes carries a confidence score measured against the principles set. Above an agreed threshold, it proceeds alone; below it, a human decides. That person’s answer is fed back into the learning loop so the next similar case clears the threshold on its own. Every decision stays transparent, auditable, and explainable—which is what I call a glass box.Fix context before you govern. You cannot govern a system that cannot see the whole picture. Ask your best employee about a project, and they will pull together the budget, the contract clause, and the customer’s last complaint because they know it all by heart. Most enterprise AI fails that test, because the information sits scattered across applications that store it in incompatible formats. I describe the full loop as Connections, Context, Reasoning, Actions, and Governance (CCRAG).Connections feed in raw information such as transactions and service records. Context weaves it into a context graph, which is a single connected picture of the business that gives agents something close to memory. Reasoning makes the decisions. Actions carry them back into the business systems. Governance keeps things aligned with the company’s intent.Most organizations obsess over the reasoning in the middle and underinvest in context and governance, which is exactly where humans play a role. Context compounds: Every interaction makes the graph richer and harder to reproduce.Learn to lead by exception. The most important change in habit comes last. Most of us have been trained to check every report and every number because we never knew where an error could surface. In a governed system, the machine tells you which cases it could not resolve confidently. Routine workflows go untouched, and your attention goes to the small portion that is ambiguous, unfamiliar, or high stakes.At first, that might feel like losing control, but it is the opposite. It is what makes a self-scaling enterprise possible, an organization whose output grows without its head count growing in proportion. People were not removed from the loop; they were raised above it.The identity questionWhen I talk with people about the shift, their resistance is rarely about technical issues. More often it is about identity: If the AI does the doing, what do I do?I have watched capable people freeze on that question. I’ve also asked myself the question.Doing was never really the job, though. Judgment was. Doing was just how we expressed it.AI has not made judgment less valuable. It has made it the scarcest resource in the organization because, for the first time, one person’s judgment, written down well, can guide thousands of decisions each day.Judgment has a twin we talk less about: taste. Judgment tells you whether an answer is sound. Taste tells you whether the question was worth asking and which of a hundred defensible options to offer the customer. A machine will happily generate all 100 options, but it cannot tell you which is best.The AI transition rewards instincts many IEEE members already have: systems thinking, precision about requirements, and honesty about failure modes. The tools have changed, but the discipline has not.Governing is where taste and judgment stop being soft words and become the work itself.The people who treat it that way, rather than as a step away from engineering, will define the profession in the age of AI.

Entertainment.title: LEGO Revives the ‘Batman Returns’ Batmobile and The Penguin's Duck for a Brick-Built Chase
Entertainment.text: SummaryLEGO is recreating two of the most recognizable vehicles from 1992's Batman Returns in a single collectible setThe Batmobile converts into its narrow Batmissile form, mirroring its escape through Gotham City's tight spaces in the filmBatman and The Penguin minifigures complete the scene, with the villain armed with his signature umbrellaLEGO has revealed the Batman Returns Batmobile & Duck, a 672-piece set that pits the Caped Crusader's armored ride against The Penguin's oversized waterfowl. Built for ages 9 and up, the set leans on movie-accurate details and moving parts, giving fans a pair of vehicles that work as well on a display shelf as they do in a staged chase.The Batmobile is the more technical of the two builds. Its standout feature is a transformation into the Batmissile, the stripped-down configuration that lets the car squeeze through narrow passages in Gotham City, a direct nod to one of the film's most memorable sequences. A cockpit sized for the Batman minifigure lets him slot in behind the wheel, and the finished car stretches more than 7.5 in. (20 cm) long and stands over 2 in. (5 cm) tall.The Duck takes a more playful approach. Wing doors swing open so The Penguin can climb inside, while both the wings and the head are posable, letting builders adjust the vehicle's expression and stance for display. The compact model measures over 4 in. (11 cm) tall and 4.5 in. (11 cm) long, and The Penguin minifigure can stand beside it with umbrella in hand when he's not behind the controls. Together, the two vehicles set up a ready-made face-off between hero and villain.The source material gives the set its pull. Directed by Tim Burton and starring Michael Keaton opposite Danny DeVito's grotesque take on The Penguin, Batman Returns has grown into a cult favorite for its gothic, holiday-season atmosphere. Its Batmobile, with the sleek, jet-inspired silhouette carried over from Burton's 1989 film, remains one of the most celebrated designs in the character's history. Pairing it with The Penguin's absurd duck vehicle captures the film's mix of menace and dark comedy in brick form.The LEGO Batman Returns Batmobile & Duck arrives January 1, 2027, via LEGO.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Flower Mountain Matches Form With Function for FW26 Collection
Entertainment.text: This season, Japanese footwear brand Flower Mountain diversifies its famously overstated sneaker library with a refined collection designed to function in both urban and rural environments. Encompassing the new drop, the brand’s popular Yamano 3 model silhouette, which typically appears in clashing colors and patterned materials, becomes pared back with technical materials that are softened through tonal palettes. The chunkier Yamabushi also gets transformed with plush leather and suede panels layered across the body.To support the styles, Flower Mountain launches a lifestyle line and a performance line, each featuring a series of brand new iterations. In the lifestyle offering, the trek-inspired Sanchia, Ranya, and Kazana Fall adopt curved lines and cushioned surfaces for a versatile look, while the Asuka 3 strips the runner silhouette of its panels and replaces them with stitched lines. Meanwhile, the performance line focuses specifically on enhancing technicality. From the straps and ties of the Back Country 2 to the Vibram-soled Iwano 2, the components bring an added layer of support and protection, as well as a touch of rugged outdoors style. Alongside the main collection, the brand also drops a special-edition capsule with the aforementioned silhouettes. Titled “Harmony of Traditions,” it looks more closely at Flower Mountain’s Japanese heritage by weaving traditional textiles like Mikawa cotton and Kurashiki canvas into an assortment of iterations. Entertainment.title: Matthieu Blazy Reimagines the Layered Legacies of Gabrielle Chanel for SS27
Entertainment.text: SummaryMatthieu Blazy presented the Chanel Spring/Summer 2027 collection exploring the evolving identities of founder Gabrielle ChanelThe runway highlighted themes of liberation backed by a soundtrack shifting from You Don't Own Me to a remix of Gimme MoreThe energetic musical transition brought a star-studded front row including Nicole Kidman Pedro Pascal and Dua Lipa to their feetChanel and Matthieu Blazy have presented the Spring/Summer 2027 collection, titled La Conversation – Part Three – Different Faces of the Same Coin. The collection examines the multi-layered history and style trajectory of founder Gabrielle Chanel, centering on the overarching theme of freedom. As guests enter the Grand Palais, they were greeted with a flock of bird-like lanterns resembling a cascade of birds in migration. The vibrantly painted floors reflected the birds aflight, just like how it would look if they flew over a the shimmering surface of a riverbed. The collection charts a course from the strictures of Edwardian corsetry to revolutionary, unconstrained suiting, leaving historical details behind as subtle remnants through lines of shadow boning, peplum flourishes, ruffled collars, and curved bodices. Blazy deconstructs masculine formal wear into raw-edged gilets, tailored trousers, and pencil-skirt suits, while 1930s-style evening gowns arrive bias-cut, sequined, or beaded with the weightless ease of a T-shirt. Lightweight flou mimics the time-lapse of cloud formations through layered silk transparencies, shifting from morning tones to nightfall.Technical innovation anchors the collection’s final chapter with the debut of "smocked tweed." Engineered as a stretch performance garment, the material adapts to the body like a second skin, delivering weightless mobility while maintaining traditional suiting aesthetics. Avian motifs—specifically swifts and swallows—appear across embroidery, hardware, and jewelry to embody freedom. Accessories cycle through time, anchored by model Dyanira Hurbuscher carrying Gabrielle’s archival 2.55 bag alongside new watch-chain flap bags, cloud-printed leather goods, and a birdcage minaudiere.The prevailing theme of liberation extended directly into the show's atmosphere. Transitioning from Lesley Gore's "You Don't Own Me" into an energetic remix of Britney Spears' "Gimme More," the soundtrack prompted the entire front row—including Nicole Kidman, Ayo Edebiri, Pedro Pascal, Kristen Wiig, Dua Lipa, and Alexa Demie—to break into dance. Entertainment.title: sacai SS27 Finds New Form in “Moment of Becoming”
Entertainment.text: Summarysacai’s SS27 “Moment of Becoming” collection explores human complexity and personal evolution through deconstructed design fractures.Structural linings are reimagined as primary silhouettes, exposing internal architecture alongside fluid, movement-reactive textiles.Sheer organza layers, exposed-mesh trench coats, and deconstructed bombers showcase a delicate balance between conviction and vulnerability.Titled "Moment of Becoming," Chitose Abe’s Spring/Summer 2027 runway collection for sacai at Paris Fashion Week delivered a poetic meditation on human evolution, authentic self-expression and quiet resolve.Abe frames the collection around human complexity, quiet resolve and personal evolution, with garments conceived as surfaces that can never fully contain the person beneath them. Instead of treating irregularity as something to disguise, SS27 gives those disruptions a central role, allowing openings, shifts in structure and exposed construction to become expressions of character rather than imperfection.The season’s most distinctive design gesture lies in the way structural linings are pulled forward to become the silhouette itself. Elements that would normally remain hidden inside a garment are elevated into defining visual features, reversing the usual hierarchy between exterior and interior.Highlighted styles include deconstructed trench coats and bomber jackets transformed with exposed mesh, sheer paneling and visible structural seams. Flowing sheer dresses and tailored trousers featuring intentional fractures and exposed linings exemplify the collection's core philosophy — capturing an unfiltered reality where vulnerability becomes an unyielding form of true strength.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Zenith and USM Return With a Mirrored DEFY Chronograph for TimeForArt
Art & Culture.text: SummaryZENITH and USM reunite for a one-off DEFY Chronograph created for TimeForArt.A mirror-polished dial combines all four signature USM colors.The watch includes a bespoke mirrored USM Haller sideboard and heads to Phillips.Following their initial collaboration in 2025, Zenith and USM have reunited to create a one-of-a-kind timepiece exclusively for TimeForArt, a benefit auction organized by the Swiss Institute. The new DEFY Chronograph USM – TimeForArt Unique Piece builds upon the architectural design of their first collaboration, which reimagined the angular 1969 DEFY, by introducing a striking, fully mirror-polished dial. This reflective surface constantly interacts with its environment, allowing the watch to change appearance based on light, movement and surrounding architecture.Set against the mirrored surface are three overlapping azuré chronograph counters accented with USM Golden Yellow, Pure Orange, Green and Gentian Blue, bringing all four signature USM colors together on a single dial for the first time. The rest of the watch retains the compact proportions and angular architecture established by the earlier collaboration, including a 37mm stainless-steel case, octagonal profile, 14-sided bezel and stainless-steel “ladder” bracelet.A miniature representation of USM Haller’s signature ball joint appears at the tip of the Gentian Blue chronograph seconds hand, creating a subtle connection between the watch and the furniture system. Powering it is ZENITH’s automatic El Primero 400 column-wheel chronograph calibre, operating at 36,000 vibrations per hour and delivering a 55-hour power reserve.Elevating the concept beyond a simple watch release, USM has designed a one-of-a-kind mirrored Haller sideboard specifically to accompany the timepiece. Conceived as a functional display for watch collectors, the furniture piece features a glass top that showcases a primary collection layer, while a lockable drawer below offers additional storage, bringing modular design language into the world of horology.The DEFY Chronograph USM – TimeForArt Unique Piece will be auctioned at Phillips New York on December 5, 2026, at 3 p.m. EST. Because it is a unique piece produced exclusively for auction, there is no official retail price; however, 100% of the proceeds will benefit the Swiss Institute's exhibitions, education initiatives, and community engagement programs.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Diptyque’s 2026 Holiday Collection Brings a Wooden Wonderland to Life
Art & Culture.text: SummaryDiptyque partners with artist Jean-Simon Roch for "The Enchanted Forest," a collection centered on wood.The seasonal pine tree scent returns across green glass candles, tapers and room sprays.Features a toolbox-inspired Advent Calendar, wooden top  and dark-wood oval labels.Diptyque steps into an "Enchanted Forest" for its 2026 Holiday Collection, imagining a winter world where carved creatures stir to life beneath a star-filled night sky. Created in collaboration with French designer and craftsman Jean-Simon Roch, the collection transforms wood into an animated, kinetic ballet of forest fauna and flora under a starry winter sky.At the center of that olfactory forest is "Sapin," Diptyque’s returning seasonal Pine Tree fragrance. Siberian fir and balsam fir give the scent the cool green snap of freshly cut branches, while cedarwood adds the dry warmth of bark and timber and moss settles underneath like a damp forest floor. Together, the notes conjure the moment a tree is first carried indoors: resin clinging to the hands, cold outdoor air still caught between its needles, then gradually warming beside candlelight.That scent story expands into Classic, Small and Very Large candles, an "Advent" taper shaped like a pine tree, a scented oval, miniature room spray and even Jean-Simon Roch’s hand-turned perfumed wooden spinning top, which releases Sapin as it moves. Elsewhere, "Feu de Bois" evokes a crackling hearth through a sculptural 2.5kg wax tree stump, while scented wax rabbits, owls and acorns bring traces of "Santal," "Baies" and "Ambre" into the collection’s miniature woodland cast.The packaging carries the same story into physical form. "Sapin" candles arrive in deep green lacquered glass scattered with gold stars and introduce a wooden interpretation of Diptyque’s signature oval label, while the Very Large edition moves into hand-enamelled ceramic with individually painted stars. The house’s "Orphéon," "Do Son" and "Eau Rose" 75ml eaux de parfum are similarly recast for the season with glittering gold lettering over black wooden oval labels, joined by larger 200ml editions of "Do Son," "Fleur de Peau" and "Orphéon."Even the Advent Calendar is conceived like a wood-turner’s toolbox, opening onto 25 fragrances, candles, body-care pieces and home objects as though revealing drawers in an artisan’s workshop. The collection rolls out through Diptyque’s boutiques, counters and online store this holiday season, with festive in-store programming beginning October 20, 2026.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: The Chinese Library’s Fall Menu Leans Into Richer Regional Chinese Flavors
Art & Culture.text: SummaryOne-Diamond restaurant The Chinese Library debuts its new seasonal menu in Hong Kong.Executive Chef Junno Li highlights clay pot braised eel, king crab dumplings, and seasonal desserts.Offerings complement signatures like Imperial Peking Duck and Manuka honey-glazed BBQ pork.Set within Hong Kong's historic Police Headquarters at Tai Kwun, The Chinese Library has officially welcomed the fall season with a new culinary collection crafted by Executive Chef Junno Li. Recognized with One Diamond in the Black Pearl Restaurant Guide for three consecutive years (2024 – 2026) and recently named among Time Out's Best Restaurants of 2026, the dining destination is renowned for celebrating the breadth of China's diverse regional cuisines.The new seasonal menu features a selection of hearty and delicate dishes designed to complement the changing weather. Standout additions include a bubbling Braised Eel with Shiso Leaves and Fermented Black Beans in a clay pot, alongside a punchy Braised Pork Neck paired with black vinegar and house spices. For lighter, comforting profiles, diners can explore the Simmered Radish in Chicken Broth with Hunan Smoked Pork or the Braised Alaskan King Crab Meat with Bamboo Fungus.Chef Junno has also introduced new dim sum creations, such as the Alaskan King Crab Dumpling and a Steamed Winter Melon Soup Dumpling, which are complemented by refreshing seasonal desserts like a Dark Chocolate Mousse with Salted Lemon Sorbet and a playful Melon Ice-Cream with Seaweed Jelly.While the seasonal additions highlight Chef Junno's latest innovations, The Chinese Library remains highly celebrated for its beloved signature dishes that anchor its contemporary Chinese repertoire. Guests frequenting the restaurant - or its popular Unlimited Dim Sum Brunch served on weekends and public holidays - can indulge in timeless staples such as the Wok-fried Fish Maw with Mushroom, the deeply flavorful BBQ Pork Loin Glazed with New Zealand Manuka Honey, and the show-stopping Roasted 45-day Imperial Peking Duck. The venue's dim sum mainstays, including the Wagyu Beef and Black Pepper Puffs and Black Truffle Har Gau, continue to showcase the kitchen's meticulous craftsmanship and dedication to elevating classic Hong Kong dining traditions.The Chinese LibraryBlock 01, Tai Kwun, Police Headquarters,10 Hollywood Rd, Central, Hong KongClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

In health and youth, only small numbers of immune cells from the body pass in the brain, but this number increases considerably with advancing age and the presence of neurodegenerative disease. The blood-brain barrier leaks, and immune cells from the body finding their way into the brain in ever greater numbers are thought to maladaptively promote inflammation, causing dysfunction and damage in brain tissue.
